title: Style with reusable CSS
learningObjectives: Complete style with reusable css using the project's existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and engineering practices.

understand.concept: Reusable CSS separates component structure from visual tokens and layout rules. Custom properties can define shared colours and spacing; component classes can provide consistent card, navigation, and button styles.
understand.whyItMatters: Reusable styles reduce duplication and make a project easier to revise. Avoid overly specific selectors and test responsive behaviour as components are reused.
understand.analogy: A shared style token is like a common measurement used by every part of a building.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; project requirements and release quality must be verified against the actual implementation and user needs.

explain.narrative: The card and button reuse shared tokens and component classes instead of repeating declarations.

examples.explanation: The card and button reuse shared tokens and component classes instead of repeating declarations.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates a project planning or implementation concept; learners must integrate and test it in their project.

practise.guidedTask: Create tokens for colour, spacing, and radius. Apply them to at least three components and verify the page at narrow and wide widths.
practise.independentTask: Complete the task in a project repository. Keep the scope explicit, preserve user privacy, test the main workflow, and document evidence and known limitations.
hints: Plan before coding and keep changes focused.
Use semantic HTML and reusable responsive CSS.
Test keyboard access, edge cases, and deployment behaviour.
